sentences.why: No source document frames the summer as a debate over 'when the first cut would land' — every Sept 2-3 source discusses hike odds (68%/60%), not a cut debate.

sentences.span: the 10-year Treasury rate hit levels last seen January last year ... yield on a Bloomberg gauge of global sovereign bonds ... highest since mid-2008
sentences.why: The 'since before 2008' record belongs to the separate global sovereign bond gauge; the source explicitly says the 10-year Treasury itself only matches January-2025 levels, a much smaller record. Corroborated by 15174: '10-year US Treasury yield rose to 4.79%, the highest level since January 2025.'

sentences.span: an investor who bought 10-year Treasuries at the yield peak of 4.99% in October 2023 would have earned a total return of more than 16% by now
sentences.why: DB's Jim Reid: normalization after 2010s financial repression, and the Oct-2023 yield-peak (price-low) purchase earned >16% — matches 'late-2023 low ... about 16%'.

sentences.span: Investors were demanding a larger fiscal-risk premium ... AI investment boom is both the equity bull case and the duration bear case
sentences.why: Deficits, energy (oil-driven selloff) and AI capex crowding out savings are all named as the structural bear case for bonds.

sentences.span: the market is at a 68% probability of a hike, despite Warsh's hawkish tone
sentences.why: A live, priced (68%/60% depending on source) hike probability at the next FOMC meeting is the front-and-center near-term event across sources.

sentences.span: Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed September rate-hike odds to ~60%
sentences.why: Warsh's Jackson Hole hawkishness is explicitly what drove hike odds up; a softer tone or a missed hike are the source-consistent invalidation conditions, reasonably synthesized.

sentences.span: Domestic AI compute demand is likely to show an ~80% CAGR
sentences.why: JPMorgan's own figure for China's domestic AI compute demand growth; paired with Goldman's 'AI infrastructure: still the main driver of EPS growth' (15122).

sentences.span: notable strength in ISG margins (15.0% v. GSe 11.7%) ... GIR remains BUY rated
sentences.why: Dell's ISG (server/infra) segment margin of 15.0% and Goldman's reiterated Buy match exactly.

sentences.span: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3% for first time since 1996 ... Expectations for a higher terminal policy rate and earlier Bank of Japan (BoJ) rate hikes
sentences.why: First-time-since-1996 figure matches; the BoJ terminal-rate debate ('the trade is fading how far BOJ goes') tracks the sourced discussion of how far BoJ hikes go.

No source states the mechanism that higher JGB yields reduce Japanese investors' incentive to hold US assets and pull money home; this causal claim isn't found anywhere in the source set, including the DB FX note and UBS Japan pieces that discuss JGB yields without this repatriation-flow claim.

sentences.span: Data show Strait of Hormuz crossings have been contracting of late
sentences.why: Transitional framing sentence with no standalone factual claim beyond pointing to the supply data discussed immediately after (s12/s13), which is sourced.

sentences.span: actual oil exports from the Persian Gulf are 40% above the March trough on a rise of dark crossings
sentences.why: Exact match, correctly attributed to Goldman's GOAL team.

sentences.span: anywhere from 2 million to 4 million barrels/day getting through versus the US administration's claim of 8m-10m b/d
sentences.why: 2-4m vs 8-10m matches exactly; JPM's own briefing (15214) separately logs '18m barrels of oil through SoH (record day)', which is 'far above' the 8-10m administration claim.

No source calls a Long $USO or $XLE trade — the only appearance of XLE in the corpus is a Goldman boilerplate disclosure line, not a trade call. This is an invented house position, which the pulse's own voice contract prohibits.

sentences.span: September and October have been the worst months for the global bond index over the last decade, with the gauge losing more than 1% on average in each of the two months
sentences.why: Source says >1% lost in EACH month (so ~2%+ combined), not 'about 1% across those two months' — magnitude roughly halved. The stat is also credited there to 'data compiled by Bloomberg,' not to Goldman or JPMorgan as the pulse attributes it.
